FINDING (spec-level gap, not a backlog item): requirement #5 -- a downloadable, commit-traceable, signed release APK -- cannot be satisfied by ANY role currently in this run's spec. The live role set is devsystem.plan, devsystem.android_native_bridge, devsystem.document_extraction, devsystem.android_emulator_test, devsystem.review. android_native_bridge writes app code; android_emulator_test exercises an already-installed app; review evaluates submitted work; document_extraction reads documents. None of them owns producing, signing, checksumming and publishing a build artifact. So #5's five acceptance criteria (APK downloadable from this run's own UI; build metadata identifying the exact CADS-webconference-demo commit SHA + versionName/versionCode; SHA-256 recorded next to the artifact; signed and installable via adb install on a clean emulator; honest failure state when the build fails) have no owner and will stay 0/5 no matter how many iterations the existing roles submit. It also blocks requirement #1 in practice: an automated emulator test needs an installable artifact before it can install anything.

HARD BLOCKER (verified, not assumed): this pipeline has nowhere to put a build artifact, so criteria 1-3 are not merely undone, they are structurally unsatisfiable today. Evidence:
- An iteration record in this run has exactly seven fields: feedback, iteration, proposals, requirement_indices, run_id, stage, succeeded. Verified as the union of keys across all 16 existing iterations via this site's own GET /api/runs/webconference-android (state.history). There is no artifact, file, url, checksum or build-metadata field.
- The run state itself (state.*) has no artifacts collection either.
- The control panel client contains zero occurrences of "artifact", "apk", "checksum" or "sha256". The only upload surface in the entire app is the Docs Search (RAG) document ingest, which is a text index for retrieval, not a per-run binary artifact store with a download control.

Consequence per acceptance criterion of #5:
- c1 (concrete APK file, downloadable from this run's own UI): unsatisfiable -- no artifact record and no download surface exist.
- c2 (build metadata identifying the exact source commit SHA and versionName/versionCode): expressible only as prose inside this feedback field, i.e. exactly the "trust the iteration text" that #5 was written to eliminate. Not machine-checkable, so I am not claiming it as met.
- c3 (SHA-256 recorded next to the artifact): "next to the artifact" cannot exist while there is no artifact record.
- c4 (signed APK, adb install on a clean emulator): blocked downstream of c1 -- devsystem.android_emulator_test has nothing to fetch and install.
- c5 (honest failure state when no APK can be produced, and not marked succeeded): this iteration is that path, exercised for real.

Requirement #5 stays 0/5. succeeded is deliberately FALSE: no APK was produced, and #5's own criterion 5 says an iteration that cannot produce one must surface an honest failure state and must not be marked succeeded. This is that honest failure, not a rubber stamp, and it intentionally consumes one of this run's 3 consecutive-failure budget rather than misreporting the state.

SEPARATE INCONSISTENCY worth reconciling by whoever owns #5: requirement #5's text names the "CADS-webconference-demo" source commit, but this run's repo_url points at CADS-webconference-android. Two different repository names for the same traceability claim -- one of them is wrong and a reviewer cannot tell which.

UNBLOCK CONDITION for this role (what the platform must add before any build-CI iteration can honestly claim #5): an artifact record attached to a run/iteration carrying at minimum the file or a retrievable URL, its sha256, the full source commit SHA, versionName/versionCode and the signing-key identity, plus a download control in the run UI. Until that exists this role can pin commits and define the build, but it cannot deliver its actual product. Filed as a platform gap rather than worked around, because working around it would mean pasting an unverifiable checksum into prose and calling #5 met.

Real devsystem.review iteration, submitted after winning this run's review role in the live auction (offer ad6ac446 @ 4, units 1, policy LowestFloor, undercutting the standing 10480f3b @ 5). Scope deliberately chosen as the four requirements with zero coverage that are NOT the known-blocked APK requirement: #1, #2, #3, #4. Sources: only this run's own Requirements, History, Roles and Code panels plus the public docs site. No assistant used.

BASELINE, read off this run's own Requirements panel: #0 addressed by iteration 15, #5 by iterations 16 and 17, and #1/#2/#3/#4 all read "not yet addressed by any iteration". Across all six requirements, 0 of 23 acceptance criteria are confirmed after 17 iterations.

FINDING 1 -- #1 is already contradicted by this run's own history, and is unenforceable as written. #1 says an iteration submitted for requirement 0 SHALL be validated by an automated Android emulator test before that iteration can be marked succeeded. Iteration 15 IS an iteration submitted for requirement 0 and it IS marked succeeded (ok), while devsystem.android_emulator_test has 0 iterations and no such test exists. Either the gate is already broken, or "succeeded" does not mean what #1 assumes -- and it does not: on this platform succeeded records whether the iteration's own work was completed, not whether the requirement is met. Iteration 15 is exactly that case, an honest review that succeeded at reporting requirement 0 is NOT met. #1 conflates the two, so no implementation can satisfy it without redefining succeeded for every stage in the run. Recommend #1 be rewritten to gate requirement 0's VERIFICATION (confirmation of its acceptance criteria) on the emulator test, rather than gating any iteration's succeeded flag. Not fixed here: rewriting a requirement is devsystem.plan's job, not review's.

FINDING 2 -- #2 and #3 restate each other's criteria but assume two different, mutually exclusive architectures. Both demand end-to-end encryption of a 1:1 message under a per-session key no intermediary can derive; #2 c1/c2 and #3 c1/c2/c3 are near-restatements of one another. Their system models differ, though: #2 is written against the CADS-Tunnel broker plus :443-relay topology, where the intermediary only forwards ("neither the broker nor any relay hop can read or tamper"), while #3 c3/c4 assume a backend that STORES ciphertext and QUEUES a message for an offline recipient ("the server stores ciphertext only", "does not require the recipient to be online"). The path shipped today is direct peer-to-peer with no store-and-forward at all, so #3 c4 cannot be met by it even in principle, and nothing anywhere in this run records which of the two architectures was chosen. A reviewer therefore cannot verify either requirement, no matter what gets implemented. Recommend: decide store-and-forward yes/no first, then either merge #2 and #3 into one encryption requirement plus a separate offline-delivery requirement, or explicitly scope #2 to the transport hop and #3 to queued/at-rest state.

FINDING 3 -- #3 may already be partly satisfied by shipped code that no iteration has ever claimed. Iteration 15 reports a real, hermetically tested Noise_IK direct peer-to-peer session in native-bridge (ct_common::a2a, genuine AEAD-authenticated handshake, real encrypted TextMessage exchange). If that report is accurate, #3's criteria 1-3 are plausibly already substantially met for the direct-address path, yet #3 shows 0/4 and "not yet addressed by any iteration" purely because nobody ever claimed it. I am deliberately NOT confirming those criteria: I did not read that code myself in this iteration, and a review must not verify a requirement from another iteration's prose. Flagged so the next devsystem.android_native_bridge iteration claims #3 explicitly instead of leaving real work invisible to this run's own coverage.

FINDING 4 -- #4 is the only sensible next implementation target. Of the uncovered requirements, #1 needs a rewrite (finding 1), #2 and #3 need an architecture decision first (finding 2), and #5 is blocked by this platform having no artifact channel at all. #4 (real per-message sent/delivered/read status, an honest error state on failure, live updates without manual refresh) depends on none of those: it is app-local UI over the existing message path, and all 5 of its criteria are checkable on one device pair without downloading any artifact. Recommend it as the next bounded increment.

VERDICT: none of #1, #2, #3, #4 is met, 0 of their acceptance criteria are confirmed, and none of them should be marked verified on the strength of this iteration. succeeded=true refers to this review's own work being complete, not to the requirements being satisfied.

TASKING: iteration 18 (devsystem.review) handed devsystem.plan two jobs -- (a) rewrite requirement #1 so it gates requirement #0's VERIFICATION rather than any iteration's succeeded flag, and (b) decide the store-and-forward question that makes #2 and #3 mutually exclusive. (a) turns out to be impossible on this platform. (b) is decided below.

FINDING 1 -- (a) CANNOT BE DONE: a requirement is immutable once created. There is no edit path and no delete path for a requirement, or for one of its acceptance criteria, anywhere in this system. Verified three independent ways, not assumed:
- This control panel's Requirements panel renders exactly three interactive controls per requirement -- requirement-toggle (the overall verified flag), criterion-toggle (per acceptance criterion) and requirement-auto-judge-toggle -- plus a read-only "decision basis" disclosure. Its only other control is the "Add requirement" form. renderRequirementsPanel has no edit or remove branch at all.
- devsystem.assistant is not a workaround: the only requirement verbs in its action vocabulary as used by this client are ToggleRequirement and ToggleAcceptanceCriterion. It has the same two toggles and nothing else.
- The published REST API reference lists the complete requirement surface as POST /requirements (add), POST /requirements/{i}/toggle, POST /requirements/{i}/auto-judge/toggle, POST /requirements/{i}/criteria/{ci}/toggle and GET /requirements/export. There is no PATCH, PUT or DELETE.
This is an asymmetry rather than a deliberate immutability guarantee: this same platform lets you edit AND remove a custom panel, update AND remove a next-step draft, remove an indexed RAG document, and DELETE an entire run. A requirement -- the one object the mandatory review gate actually keys on, and what the coverage and N/M-confirmed counters score -- is the only load-bearing thing here that can never be corrected.

WHY I AM DELIBERATELY NOT "FIXING" #1 BY APPENDING A CORRECTED COPY: iteration 18 finding 1 is right and I confirm it -- on this platform succeeded records whether an iteration's own work completed, not whether a requirement is met, and iteration 15 is exactly that case (an honest review that succeeded at reporting requirement 0 is NOT met). So #1 is unsatisfiable as written. But appending a corrected requirement #6 would leave the broken #1 in the set permanently, permanently at 0/3, permanently unverifiable, still counted by coverage -- trading one wrong requirement for one wrong requirement plus a near-duplicate beside it, and guaranteeing this requirement set can never reach a fully-verified state. That is a worse spec than the one I started with. Whether to carry #1 as a known-dead entry or recreate the run (losing all 19 iterations of real history) is the operator's call, not mine to make silently. Recorded here so the decision is visible and traceable instead of worked around. Filed as scimbe/CADS-devsystem#37.

FINDING 2 -- (b) DECIDED: this run assumes a forwarding-only topology with NO ciphertext-storing backend. The decision is forced by what exists in this run, not by preference:
- The role set (plan, android_native_bridge, document_extraction, android_emulator_test, review, android_native_build_ci) contains no backend or server role. Nobody in this run owns a service that could hold a mailbox.
- repo_url is https://github.com/scimbe/CADS-webconference-android -- a client repo. There is no server repo in this run.
- Milestone M1 (achieved) is a direct CADS-Tunnel Noise_IK channel with history persisted LOCALLY. Milestone M2 -- the operator's own named next goal -- is ct-agent channel join, SignedChannelGrant, rendezvous, NAT traversal, :443 relay fallback. Every one of those is connection establishment or forwarding; none of them stores a message.
- Requirement #0 names that same mechanism, and #2 is written against that same topology ("neither the CADS-Tunnel broker nor any :443 relay hop can read or tamper").
- The backlog's open discovery item describes the broker as something a client JOINS to reach a peer, living in ct-agent/ct_edge -- not a message store.
DECISION OF RECORD FOR THIS RUN: forward-only, no store-and-forward. Messages transit; nothing queues them. #2 is this run's real encryption requirement.

CONSEQUENCE FOR #3, stated plainly because it is not recoverable: #3 c1 and c2 (on-device encryption before transmission; a fresh per-conversation session key via authenticated key exchange) describe the same property #2 c2 does and are satisfiable by the shipped Noise_IK mechanism -- iteration 18 finding 3 is right that these may already be substantially met on the direct-address path and were simply never claimed. #3 c3 ("the server stores ciphertext only") can only ever be vacuously true: there is no server, and a reviewer cannot confirm a property of a component that does not exist. #3 c4 ("does not require the recipient to be online; a queued message is encrypted before upload") is UNSATISFIABLE under this decision, by construction and permanently -- and per finding 1 it cannot be edited out. #3 can therefore never reach 4/4. Note also that #3 reads in a different vocabulary from the rest of this run -- "participant", "the server", "upload", "backend", where #0 and #2 say "Android client", "broker", "relay hop". It looks like a generic messenger requirement imported from a different system model, and that mismatch is the actual root of the #2/#3 conflict iteration 18 found.

ESCALATED TO THE OPERATOR, NOT DECIDED HERE: whether CADS-webconference should EVER support offline delivery is a product decision, not an architecture one, and it is bigger than this run. What I decided above is only this run's scope, forced by what exists in it. If the product answer is yes, it needs a new backend service, its own repo and a new role in this spec, and #3 would have to be recreated rather than amended -- which finding 1 makes messy. I do not have the standing to decide the product; I do have the evidence that this run as specified cannot deliver it.

BUDGET, because no iteration so far has factored it in: health reports iterations_completed 18 of max_iterations 20, iterations_until_ceiling 2, iterations_until_checkin 2 (the Health & Criteria panel does flag this in its danger state -- this is not a reporting gap, it is a planning fact nobody has acted on). Raising max_iterations on the Health & Criteria panel is a real, available operator action and is the prerequisite for any further real work here.

SCOPE OF THIS ITERATION: planning and decision only. It satisfies NO acceptance criteria of #1, #2 or #3 and produces no code. succeeded:true means this planning work itself was completed -- the requested rewrite was proven impossible with evidence rather than silently skipped, the store-and-forward question was decided for this run's scope with the product question escalated, and the run's remaining budget was surfaced. It does NOT mean any of these requirements is met, and none of them should be marked verified on the strength of this iteration.

RECOMMENDED NEXT, for the single remaining slot: iteration 18 named #4 (real per-message sent/delivered/read status, honest error state, live updates) as the only requirement blocked by neither the artifact gap nor the architecture question. That is still correct, and after finding 2 it is now also the only requirement whose criteria one devsystem.android_native_bridge increment could actually close. Architekt iteration: drive the stalled devsystem.android_emulator_test stage. Goal -- run an automated Android emulator test harness against the current build (commit ce4aa2c, app: close MessageStore SQLiteDatabase handle in onDestroy) to validate requirement #0 (M2 broker channel exchange) and requirement #4 (per-message sent/delivered/read status). The emulator test SHALL boot an AVD, install the built APK, exercise a 1:1 message exchange between two emulator instances over the Noise_IK direct peer-to-peer channel, and assert: (a) message payload is ciphertext on the wire (no plaintext in logs/adb traffic), (b) per-message status transitions sent->delivered->read reflect real device state, (c) no crash/onDestroy leak (MessageStore handle closed). Proposal: add an emulator-test role proposal that wires instrumented androidTest against com.scimbe.webconference, runs on a headless AVD via gradle connectedCheck, and reports pass/fail per criterion back to this run. This unblocks the test gate for the APK delivery (requirement #5 blocked by artifact channel #36, but emulator-test coverage is the prerequisite that the run can satisfy on its own).

Architekt iteration: drive the remaining stalled devsystem.document_extraction stage. Goal -- implement document text extraction so that shared documents (PDF, text, common office formats) sent in a 1:1 or group conversation are extracted to searchable text and indexed for in-app search, supporting requirement #9 (media/attachment sharing) and a future in-conversation document search. The stage SHALL extract plain text from common document MIME types, store the extracted text alongside the attachment metadata, and surface a search field that matches across all extracted document text in the current conversation. Proposal: add a document_extraction role proposal that wires an Android TextExtractor (PdfRenderer for PDF, plain text passthrough, Apache POI-ish fallback for office) producing a searchable text blob per attachment, persisted in the local MessageStore alongside the attachment row. This unblocks document content search and complements the media-sharing requirement.

Real, bounded increment on requirement #4 (per-message delivery status): implemented the first honest slice this direct, unacknowledged Noise_IK channel can actually support -- a real sent/failed status per message, not the full sent/delivered/read/live-update text. This channel has no acknowledgement protocol above the transport layer, so "the native sendText() call returned" and "it threw" are the only two states knowable today; delivered/read both need a new, real wire-level receipt message round-tripped back over the channel, deliberately not fabricated here.

Real bug found while scoping this: a failed send used to vanish completely -- no thread entry, nothing persisted, only the separate connection-status text changed, so a user had no way to tell "this specific message never went out" from "it's still somewhere in flight." Now recorded and rendered as a real FAILED entry in the thread itself.

MessageStore: new nullable status column (DB_VERSION 2, drop-and-recreate on upgrade, an acceptable stated loss of local chat history for this scaffold's current stage). insert()/loadAll() carry it through; a RECEIVED row never has one. Two new hermetic tests: status round-trips correctly for SENT/FAILED with RECEIVED honestly null, and a retried send's existing CONFLICT_REPLACE overwrites the earlier FAILED row's status too, not just its body.

MainActivity.onSendClicked persists+renders the real status either way instead of the old success-only path. New message_line_sent_failed string; message_line_sent now shows an explicit "sent" marker instead of an unmarked line, since the requirement asks for an explicit status, not an implied one.

CADS-webconference-android@7e325e6.

Security: TextMessage.sender_pubkey is self-reported by the sender at compose time, not derived from the authenticated Noise session -- harmless today since only message direction drives rendering, but a forged sender_pubkey would be silently trusted if that ever changes. Found by devsystem.assistant, 2026-08-07, reading iteration 13's own real findings; pinned here so it survives past that iteration's prose.

MessageStore never closes its SQLiteDatabase handle (no onDestroy()/close() call in MainActivity). A real fix + Robolectric test were written earlier this session but reverted before shipping (host disk headroom too tight to safely pull an Android SDK image for a hermetic test path) -- corroborated independently by devsystem.assistant, 2026-08-07. Needs a firing with more disk headroom, or a lighter verification path that does not need the full Android SDK image.

Residual scope from the sender_pubkey provenance fix (native-bridge/src/channel.rs, CADS-webconference-android@79774cd): only the dialer/initiator side overrides a received messages sender_pubkey with the real, Noise_IK-authenticated key. The listener/responder side still trusts the wire value verbatim -- ct_common::a2a::a2a_respond (CADS-Tunnel, a separate pinned repo) learns the initiators key internally during the handshake but does not return it, only the resulting TransportState. Closing this needs an upstream CADS-Tunnel change (return the authenticated peer key from a2a_respond), correctly scoped as its own separate increment. Still harmless today: nothing in the GUI trusts sender_pubkey for anything, only message direction drives rendering.

milestones.description: 1:1 Text-Messaging end-to-end: Android-Client sendet und empfängt Textnachrichten über einen CADS-Tunnel Channel (Noise_IK), Verlauf lokal persistiert

M2 -- Broker-vermittelte Kanal-Discovery: Android-Client verbindet sich über den echten CADS-Tunnel Broker (ct-agent channel join, SignedChannelGrant, Rendezvous, NAT-Traversal, :443 Relay-Fallback), ohne manuellen Public-Key/Adress-Austausch wie bei M1. Naechstes echtes Ziel nach M1 (achieved), benannt vom real deployten devsystem.assistant selbst als der natuerliche naechste Meilenstein, 2026-08-07.

requirements.statement: WHEN the Android client starts and no manual peer address/public-key has been entered, THE SYSTEM SHALL discover and connect to a peer channel via the real CADS-Tunnel broker (ct-agent channel join, SignedChannelGrant, rendezvous, NAT traversal, :443 relay fallback) instead of requiring out-of-band manual exchange.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh install with no prior manual peer entry can still exchange a real text message with a second device, using only broker-mediated discovery.
Falling back to direct-address connect (todays real M1 mechanism) remains available for a user who already has a peers public key/address.
A broker-discovery failure (no reachable peer, relay exhausted) surfaces a real, honest status message -- never a silent no-op.

requirements.statement: WHEN an iteration is submitted for requirement 0 (M2 broker-mediated channel discovery), THE SYSTEM SHALL be validated by an automated Android emulator test covering that requirement's acceptance criteria before the iteration can be marked succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: An automated emulator test exists that installs the app fresh (no manual peer entry) and exchanges a real text message with a second emulator instance using only broker-mediated discovery.
An automated emulator test exists that verifies the existing direct-address (M1) fallback connect still works unchanged.
An automated emulator test exists that simulates a broker-discovery failure (no reachable peer / relay exhausted) and asserts a real, honest status message is shown, not a silent no-op.

requirements.statement: WHEN two Android clients exchange a message over a channel established via requirement 0 (broker-mediated discovery) or the existing direct-address (M1) path, THE SYSTEM SHALL end-to-end encrypt and authenticate the message content so that neither the CADS-Tunnel broker nor any :443 relay hop can read or tamper with plaintext, and the SignedChannelGrant/rendezvous material alone SHALL NOT be sufficient to derive message content.
acceptance_criteria: Independent capture at the broker/relay hop during a real message exchange (fresh install, broker-mediated discovery per requirement 0) contains no recoverable plaintext of the message body.

Messages are protected with per-session keys established directly between the two Android clients (e.g. via a Signal-style key agreement), not derivable from the SignedChannelGrant or any broker-held material alone.
If end-to-end key agreement fails or is unavailable, the system surfaces a real, honest status message and does not silently fall back to sending unencrypted message content.

requirements.statement: WHEN a participant sends a 1:1 message, THE SYSTEM SHALL encrypt the message payload end-to-end (sender and recipient only) using a per-session key so that the server and any intermediary cannot read the content.
acceptance_criteria: 1:1 message payloads are encrypted on-device before transmission; the backend never receives plaintext message bodies.
A fresh session key is established per conversation via an authenticated key exchange; no long-term static symmetric key is reused for payload encryption.
Only the sender and the intended recipient hold the keys to decrypt a message body; the server stores ciphertext only.
Encrypting and sending a message does not require the recipient to be online; a queued message is encrypted before upload and remains ciphertext until the recipient decrypts it.

requirements.statement: WHEN a participant sends a 1:1 message, THE SYSTEM SHALL surface a real, honest per-message delivery status (sent / delivered / read or a concrete error) to the sender, so the user can tell whether the message reached the recipient and was read, instead of a silent or fake state.
acceptance_criteria: The sender UI shows a real per-message status (e.g. sent, delivered, read) reflecting the actual message state, never a stale or fabricated status.
A "delivered" indicator is only shown after the message has actually been handed to the recipient device (or honestly queued for it), not before transmission.
A "read" indicator is only shown after the recipient actually opened the message; no silent false read state.
If delivery fails (recipient unreachable, queue exhausted, timeout), the sender sees a real error/retry state, not a silent no-op or indefinite spinner.
The status updates live as the message progresses (sent -> delivered -> read) and does not require a manual refresh.

requirements.statement: WHEN an iteration for this run is marked succeeded, THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a downloadable, installable release APK artifact that is traceable to the exact source commit it was built from, so a reviewer can install it on a real device and re-verify the claimed behaviour instead of trusting the iteration text.
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline emits a concrete APK file (not only a build log) that is downloadable from this run's own UI.
The APK's recorded build metadata identifies the exact CADS-webconference-demo source commit (full SHA) and the versionName/versionCode it was built from.
A SHA-256 checksum of the APK is recorded next to the artifact so a reviewer can verify the file they downloaded is the one the pipeline built.
The APK is signed with a build key recorded in the run and installs on a clean Android emulator via `adb install` with no manual signing step.
If the build fails or no APK can be produced, the iteration surfaces a real, honest failure state and is not marked succeeded.

requirements.statement: WHEN a participant selects an image, video or document to send in a 1:1 chat, THE SYSTEM SHALL upload, transmit and render a real preview/thumbnail of the media to both sender and recipient, with honest progress and error states, so media sharing works reliably and comparably to WhatsApp/Signal instead of silently dropping or failing to render attachments.
acceptance_criteria: The sender can pick an image/video/document from the device and the chat shows a visible upload/progress indicator while the media is being transmitted.
The recipient sees a rendered preview/thumbnail of the received media inline in the conversation, not just a raw file name or empty bubble.
If media upload or transmission fails (too large, unsupported format, network error), the sender sees a real error/retry state, not a silent no-op or indefinite spinner.
The media is delivered over the same encrypted channel as text messages and is only marked sent/delivered after the recipient device actually received it.
Media metadata (dimensions, duration for video, size) is surfaced so the user can judge what was shared.

requirements.statement: WHEN a user wants to start a new 1:1 conversation, THE SYSTEM SHALL offer contact discovery from the device address book (with explicit permission) plus manual entry by phone-number/username, so the user can find and start a conversation with a real contact within seconds comparably to WhatsApp/Signal, instead of having to type opaque identifiers or guess.
acceptance_criteria: The user can grant address-book permission on first use and the app lists existing contacts who are reachable on the conference system, with names and avatars, sorted/searchable.
The user can start a new 1:1 chat directly from a discovered contact with a single tap, without copying identifiers.
The user can also manually add a contact by phone number or username and the system verifies the contact is reachable before opening a chat.
If address-book access is denied or empty, the app shows an honest empty state with a path to grant permission or add contacts manually, not a silent blank screen.
Contact discovery does not leak the full address book to other participants; only reachable contacts are surfaced to the local user.

requirements.statement: WHEN a user wants to share content beyond plain text in a 1:1 or group conversation, THE SYSTEM SHALL let the user attach and send an image, short video, document, or voice note from the device, and shall render it inline for the recipient with a real transfer progress indicator and an honest error state on failure -- comparably to WhatsApp/Signal -- instead of silently dropping the attachment or degrading to text-only.
acceptance_criteria: The user can pick an image, video, document, or record a voice note from within the conversation and send it as a real attachment, not a text-only fallback.
Recipients see the attachment rendered inline (image thumbnail, playable video/audio, downloadable document) without leaving the conversation.
A visible progress indicator shows upload/download progress for the attachment, and a clear error state with retry appears when transfer fails, instead of a silent drop or indefinite spinner.
Attachments are sent over the same encrypted channel as text messages and do not leak metadata (e.g. file names, thumbnails) beyond what the recipient already sees in the conversation.
Large attachments are handled gracefully (downscaled/compressed previews, size limits surfaced honestly) without crashing the conversation or running the app out of memory.

requirements.statement: WHEN a user wants to converse with more than one participant at once, THE SYSTEM SHALL let the user create and join a named group conversation (multi-participant, 3+ members) where every member can send and receive text/media messages broadcast to all participants, with a real member list, a group title, add/remove-member controls, and the same per-message delivery/read status and end-to-end encryption as 1:1 chats -- comparably to WhatsApp/Signal group chats -- instead of limiting the user to 1:1 conversations only.
acceptance_criteria: User can create a new named group with 3+ members from contacts/address book; group title is editable and visible to all members.
Any member can send a message that is broadcast to all current members; each recipient sees the same per-message sent/delivered/read status as in 1:1 chats.
Group membership is mutable: an admin/owner can add and remove members; removed members no longer receive new messages and cannot read future traffic.
Group messages use the same end-to-end encryption as 1:1 (no plaintext to broker/relay); a new member cannot read messages sent before they joined (forward secrecy across join boundary).
The group survives a member going offline and rejoining (group state is consistent across reconnects); leaving the group is explicit and confirmed.

requirements.statement: WHEN a participant is composing a message in a 1:1 conversation, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the remote participant a real 'typing…' indicator while the sender is actively entering text, and SHALL hide it when the sender stops or sends the message, so conversational flow feels live and comparable to WhatsApp/Signal instead of the recipient staring at a silent input with no feedback.
acceptance_criteria: While the sender is actively typing in a 1:1 chat, the recipient UI shows a real, live 'typing…' indicator (not a static/fake one).
When the sender stops typing for a bounded idle window (e.g. a few seconds) or sends/cancels the message, the 'typing…' indicator disappears on the recipient side, not stuck on.
The indicator is per-conversation and does not leak across conversations or appear for senders who are not actually typing.
When the channel is down or the peer is unreachable, the indicator does not falsely show 'typing…' on the recipient side (no fabricated presence).
The indicator works over the same real channel as messages (broker-discovery or direct-address) and does not require a separate manual connection.

requirements.statement: WHEN the Android client is in the background or the screen is off and a new 1:1 or group message arrives that the user has not yet seen, THE SYSTEM SHALL surface a real OS-level push notification (with sender name/number and a message preview that respects end-to-end-encryption by decrypting locally before display) so the user is alerted to the message comparably to WhatsApp/Signal, instead of silently dropping the notification or only updating the in-app UI the user cannot see.
acceptance_criteria: When a new 1:1 or group message arrives while the app is backgrounded or the screen is off, the device shows a real OS-level notification (notification channel, sound/vibration per system settings) containing the sender display name and a short preview of the message body.

The notification preview is produced by decrypting the message locally on-device (end-to-end-encrypted content is decrypted with the user's key before display); no plaintext is leaked to the OS notification surface beyond what the user's own device already holds.
Tapping the notification opens the app directly to the conversation that produced the message, not a generic inbox or the last-opened screen.

If the OS grants a restricted/background-execution budget that is too small to fetch and decrypt the message (e.g. Doze, battery saver), the app shows an honest, non-fabricated notification ('New message from <sender>' without a preview body) rather than fabricating a preview it never decrypted or silently dropping the notification.

The user can mute a specific 1:1 or group conversation so that its messages do NOT raise an OS-level push notification while still being delivered inside the app, and the mute setting persists across app restarts.
